## 固定收益開盤主論述

美國就業報告遠優於預期，6月5日美債逆轉前一交易日的漲勢，政策敏感的前端殖利率大幅上揚，交易員並已完全反映聯準會年底前升息。5月非農就業增加17.2萬人，高於所有預測；3月及4月新增就業均上修，失業率則維持4.3%。能源成本居高不下、使通膨持續高於聯準會目標之際，就業成長範圍擴大，也動搖了經濟正進入低聘僱均衡的看法。

2年期殖利率上升10.3個基點至4.148%，5年期上升8.4個基點至4.269%，10年期上升5.6個基點至4.531%，30年期則上升2.1個基點至4.997%。前端領跌使2年期與10年期利差收窄4.7個基點至38.3個基點，2年期與30年期利差收窄8.2個基點至84.9個基點。這種曲線變化顯示，眼前衝擊集中在預期政策路徑，而非市場因財政供給或持續通膨而重新要求長端讓利。

10年期殖利率的拆解進一步支持這項判讀。實質殖利率上升7.1個基點至2.162%，漲幅超過名目殖利率；10年期損益兩平通膨率則下降1.5個基點至2.369%。WTI原油下跌2.69%至$90.54，布蘭特原油下跌2.04%至$93.09，因此即使就業報告推升投資人要求的實質利率，通膨補償仍能回落。這波賣壓並非能源驅動型通膨交易的簡單延續；非農數據顯示需求足以承受當前借貸成本，壓縮聯準會淡化價格衝擊的空間。

調整幅度遠超公債市場。美元指數上漲0.66%，黃金期貨下跌3.10%，標普500指數下跌2.64%，Nasdaq 100下跌4.77%；費城半導體指數重挫10.26%，VIX則大漲近40%至21.51。科技股劇烈下跌不只反映非農意外，投資人也在質疑偏高的AI估值，以及建設所需資金規模。實質殖利率走高，促使市場全面重估對遠期現金流敏感的股票風險。

克里夫蘭聯準銀行總裁Beth Hammack表示，就業報告再次確認勞動市場大致均衡，4.3%的失業率接近她所定義的充分就業。鑑於不確定性，她仍主張維持利率不變，但也重申，若近期趨勢持續，可能很快就適合採取行動。數據提高了這項附帶條件警告的分量，但預測機構對下一步是否真會升息仍有分歧。法國巴黎銀行預測12月起連續升息三次；花旗仍預期2026年降息三次；高盛則取消原先預期的2026年最後一次降息，但未將升息列為基本情境。

因此，收盤行情一方面反映明確的短期重新定價，另一方面仍未解決中期政策爭論。就業成長更廣、前期數字上修，加上消費者借款穩健，使勞動市場疲弱不再是支持降息的有力理由；然而油價與損益兩平通膨率下跌，也顯示投資人並未直接把最新能源衝擊外推為長期通膨。下一步要看5月消費者及生產者物價能否支持市場新反映的緊縮路徑，以及總額$1,190億的附息債標售期間，美債需求能否維持有序。

## 就業成長範圍擴大，聯準會路徑重新定價

5月非農就業增加17.2萬人，遠高於公布前8.8萬人的預測中位數，前兩個月數字也雙雙上修。三個月合計創下逾兩年來最強的聘僱增幅。這一連串數據比單月優於預期的頭條更重要，因為勞動市場圖像已從就業近乎停滯，轉為連續數份報告均顯示動能增強。

失業率維持4.3%，勞動參與率持平於61.8%，25至54歲主要工作年齡人口的參與率則微升。包含氣餒勞工及因經濟因素從事兼職者的廣義失業指標下降。這些數據幾乎沒有跡象顯示，非農就業增加掩蓋了勞動供給惡化或就業不足加劇。

聘僱也不再像先前經濟疲弱期間般集中於防禦型服務業。休閒與餐旅業增加7萬個職位，為逾三年最多，主要由餐廳及酒吧帶動；醫療保健與社會救助業持續穩健擴張，製造業也增聘人員，非住宅營建就業則連續第七個月增加。

部分強勁表現可能只是暫時現象。經濟學家指出，為6月及7月FIFA世界盃所做的準備可能拉高休閒與餐旅業就業，賽事結束後相關聘僱可能放緩或回吐。大型科技公司一面裁員、一面投入更多資金建設AI基礎設施，使資訊業就業在過去17個月中第16度下降。小型企業此前也在縮減聘僱計畫，消費者對職缺多寡的評估仍弱於近年。

不過，5月的關鍵在於這些保留因素並未蓋過整體改善。資料中心、國防生產及預防性備貨相關的工廠需求支撐製造業。4月資料中心營建支出折合年率首次突破$500億，占全美營建支出的2.3%。因此，非住宅營建增聘進一步連結資本投資熱潮與勞動市場，並非僅反映住宅或公共工程活動。

美債立即作出反應。數據公布後，2年期殖利率盤中上升約11個基點至4.15%，之後一度觸及4.17%；當日收在4.148%，仍較前一日高10.3個基點，較一個月前高20.5個基點。5年期同樣承受大部分調整，殖利率曲線因而趨平；交易員也從原先認為年底升息機率很高，轉為完全反映升息25個基點。

利率交換顯示，10月升息的機率約為60%，但完整的25個基點直到12月會議才完全反映。這項區別很重要，因為市場仍普遍預期6月16日至17日會議將把聯邦基金利率目標維持在3.5%至3.75%。眼前焦點與其說是聯準會會否在6月升息，不如說聲明是否移除寬鬆傾向，並為後續會議明確建立雙向政策路徑。

就業報告改變了這項溝通難題。先前證據包括初領失業救濟金人數增加、服務業調查的就業指標萎縮，以及低聘僱、低解僱的環境。5月非農並未推翻所有偏弱指標，但前期上修及產業分布改善，使就業即將急劇惡化更難成為基本情境。決策官員如今可更直接聚焦通膨，而不致被認為忽視迅速轉弱的就業使命。

當日稍晚公布的消費者信用，則提供另一項需求與家庭資產負債表訊號。4月借款增加$207.3億，高於市場共識的$178億；3月增幅修正為$222.3億。消費者信用餘額達$5.1531兆，折合年率成長4.8%；循環信用成長10.4%，非循環信用則成長2.9%。

循環借款加速並不必然代表需求強勁，因為所得成長不足時，家庭也可能更依賴信用。即便如此，數據仍顯示無擔保融資管道持續暢通，家庭借款也未驟然收縮。與就業結果合併來看，在下一批通膨數據公布前，聯準會尚未取得明確的需求破壞訊號。

美債成交量也反映重新定價的規模。FINRA記錄429,057筆交易，面額活動達$1.174兆，總面額成交量較前一日增加12.9%。名目附息債活動增加24.3%至$9,992億。剩餘期限逾3年至5年的附息債成交量增加39.7%至$2,779億，為各細分期限中增幅最大；2年以下增加18.8%，7至10年期增加18.4%。交易集中度證實政策敏感的曲線中段是調整核心，但無法判定客戶為淨買方或淨賣方。

每週期貨資料顯示，這次重新定價發生在多空部位龐大對峙的市場，而非方向共識明確的環境。截至6月2日，資產管理機構在各類美債期貨均持有大量淨多單，槓桿基金則大幅淨放空。一週內，資產管理機構的5年期與10年期期貨淨部位分別增加190,077口及283,949口，槓桿基金則將5年期淨空單增加186,242口。這些部位早於非農報告，無法判斷週五資金流向，但足以說明為何重大數據意外能迅速引發整條曲線調整。

## 實質殖利率引發劇烈風險反轉

儘管市場較廣泛的通膨疑慮仍源自中東能源衝擊，美債賣壓主要由實質殖利率主導。10年期實質殖利率升至2.162%，一個月上升21.8個基點；同期10年期損益兩平通膨率反而下降11.2個基點至2.369%。經濟活動展現韌性、推高預期政策利率，使投資人要求更高的通膨調整後報酬，但要求的長期通膨補償不是上升，而是下降。

油價回落促成這項分化。WTI收在$90.54，布蘭特收在$93.09，兩者全週仍上漲。當日跌勢減輕眼前的通膨衝擊，卻未解決衝突造成的能源供應中斷。這也意味非農數據，而非原油再次單日上漲，最能解釋當日美債走勢。

2年期與30年期利差收窄8.2個基點尤其具有指標意義。市場報導顯示，30年期殖利率盤中一度重返5%以上，最終僅上升2.1個基點，收在4.997%。若當日主要反映新的財政、供給或長期通膨衝擊，長端理應承受更大壓力；實際上，跌幅最重的仍是受預期聯準會政策最直接影響的期限。

實質利率重新定價，直接衝擊高度依賴長期成長假設的股市。截至6月5日前，Nasdaq 100自3月30日以來已上漲逾30%；當日重挫4.77%，為2025年4月以來最差表現，半導體指數下跌10.26%，抹去大部分全週漲幅。標普500資訊科技類股下跌5.8%，但11個類股中仍有5個上漲，由民生消費與公用事業領先。這種分化顯示資金正在撤離昂貴的科技部位，而非成長預期全面崩塌。

個別企業疑慮進一步放大跌勢。Broadcom營收預測令投資人失望；另有報導稱Meta Platforms正考慮增資，使市場再次質疑，即便規模最大的科技公司，是否也能以內部資金支應AI投資週期。同一天，實質殖利率上升提高遠期獲利的折現率，非農報告又降低近期貨幣政策轉鬆的可能性，讓這些疑慮同時發酵。

風險減碼也擴及其他資產。實質利率上升與美元走強的影響壓過黃金的避險角色，黃金期貨下跌3.10%至$4,337.10。比特幣盤中跌破$60,000，為2024年10月以來首次。美元指數升至100.07，就業數據公布後，G10貨幣全數兌美元走弱。

上市信用債基金也下跌，但並未出現科技股同等程度的失序。投資級債基金LQD下跌0.62%，高收益債基金HYG與JNK分別下跌0.50%及0.44%，新興市場債基金EMB下跌0.73%。這些報酬同時包含利率敏感度及標的信用風險的影響，不能據此認定利差全面變動；但它們顯示，在美債殖利率上升、股市下跌之際，固定收益風險資產也未能倖免。

## Warsh面對加速升溫的政策辯論

Hammack的回應明確把非農報告納入聯準會反應函數。她認為勞動市場大致均衡，並稱4.3%的失業率接近充分就業。鑑於不確定性，維持利率不變仍屬合理，但若近期趨勢延續，可能很快便有理由採取行動。這項條件與她本週稍早的發言相同；新增資訊在於非農已明顯朝更容易滿足該條件的方向發展。

因此，主席Kevin Warsh上任後首次會議不能只是波瀾不驚地維持利率。4月會議紀錄顯示，多數官員認為，如果通膨持續高於2%，可能需要考慮升息。先前支持寬鬆的理事Lisa Cook與Christopher Waller近期也表示，通膨正朝錯誤方向發展，最終可能需要提高利率。5月就業結果削弱了以勞動市場為由反對政策轉向的論點。

Warsh就任後尚未公開闡述政策立場。獲提名前，他以抗通膨鷹派聞名，但也曾主張應降息，並指出有若干力量可在較長期間支持借貸成本下降。他必須在6月記者會上調和這段經歷與當前經濟現況：聘僱轉強，聯準會偏好的通膨指標4月達3.8%，為2023年以來最高。

會議發布的經濟預測將構成另一項溝通考驗。相較3月預測，新的通膨與利率假設可能較高，但現有證據不足以判斷多少官員會預測升息，以及升息時點。就業報告使決策者更容易移除偏向降息的措辭，卻不足以決定委員會是否會採取明確的緊縮傾向。

華爾街目前的預測反映異常分歧的政策反應函數。法國巴黎銀行預期聯準會12月開始升息，連續升息三次，最終全數收回2025年降息75個基點的寬鬆幅度。該行認為，若勞動市場保持強勁、伊朗衝突使通膨延續，也可能更早啟動。這項預測把先前寬鬆視為一種保險；一旦經濟韌性超出預期，便可能需要撤回。

花旗維持相反看法。美國首席經濟學家Andrew Hollenhorst預期勞動市場未來三個月轉弱，促使聯準會在9月、10月及12月各降息25個基點。花旗承認，非農公布後，官員在6月會更重視通膨上行風險，但主張目前的強勢不會持續。

高盛週五報告的立場介於兩者之間。該行取消原先預期的2026年12月降息，並把最後兩次預期降息延至2027年6月及12月。小幅升息的機率由10%上調至20%，但因通膨似乎較不可能形成自我延續趨勢，仍認為升息機率不高。高盛只給予2027年降息兩次的新基本情境30%的機率，並把長期維持利率不變列為合理替代情境；2026年失業率預測也由4.6%下修至4.4%。

各家歧見不只取決於下一份通膨數據。法國巴黎銀行看到的是強勁經濟，可能迫使聯準會收回先前寬鬆；花旗預期勞動市場疲弱重新浮現；高盛則認為通膨受抑程度足以避免升息，但經濟又不夠弱，不足以支持2026年降息。非農使市場向第一種觀點靠攏，損益兩平通膨率及油價下降，則為後兩種情境保留空間。

收盤後，政治壓力更趨明確。美國總統Donald Trump在週五錄製、週日播出的訪問中表示，聯準會若升息將是錯誤決定，反而應該降息。他主張不應自動以緊縮政策懲罰經濟成功，並把降低利率的偏好與聯邦債務及擴大軍事支出的計畫連結。訪問在完整交易時段結束後才播出，因此不是週五重新定價的原因，卻加深了Warsh首次會議面臨的制度考驗：市場轉向反映緊縮，提名他的總統卻公開要求相反政策。

## 信用市場支應AI，困境企業推動重整

科技股賣壓並未阻止大型AI相關融資完成。Apollo Global Management與Blackstone敲定一筆$350億融資，用以購買Google設計、將由Anthropic承租的晶片，是迄今規模最大的私募信貸交易之一。約半數債務分銷予外部投資人，顯示即使交易由大型另類資產管理機構發起，仍需龐大的機構需求支撐。

融資分為三個不同風險層級。$60億A1層出售給銀行，票息為美債殖利率加1個百分點；$240億A2層以面額定價，票息5.75%，買方包括Apollo旗下保險公司Athene等機構投資人。兩個優先層級均取得私下評定的中段投資級評等，並獲Broadcom付款支持。

其餘$45億B票據沒有Broadcom支持，以面額定價，票息8.5%。相較A2票息高出275個基點，反映投資人對額外保障的重視，但各層級也可能存在其他結構差異。交易的經濟基礎主要取決於特殊目的載體所持晶片產生的租金，以及Anthropic未能付款時晶片的剩餘價值。

Broadcom對優先債務的支持正是為處理剩餘價值風險。如果租金在指定期間內停止支付，該載體可出售晶片；Broadcom同意補足出售後對A1及A2投資人的剩餘欠款，最高可達受保障金額的100%。B票據不享有這項支持。此結構使優先層的借款條件更接近Broadcom的信用狀況，次順位投資人則直接承擔專用硬體價值及Anthropic履行租約的風險。

市場預期，這是Broadcom、Apollo、Blackstone及其他投資人參與的AI基礎設施平台所安排的首批交易之一。Broadcom表示，平台目標是在2028年前部署超過20吉瓦的運算容量。這項潛在融資管線對固定收益市場意義重大，因為它把股市的成長題材轉化為銀行資產負債表、私募信貸、保險資本及結構型債務的持續融資需求。

市政債投資人則提供另一條科技相關融資管道。Alphabet與Pioneer Community Energy參與、規模約$10億的預付能源債券完成定價後，次級市場需求強勁。債券由California Community Choice Financing Authority發行，高盛承銷，Alphabet則在預付電力安排中擔任金融中介。

最大一部分債券最初以高於基準95個基點定價，隨後交易利差收窄；僅2035年到期券截至週五下午的成交額便達$4.92億。該批債券平均成交利差為89個基點，部分交易最窄達74個基點。這項結果顯示，Alphabet涉足預付能源融資已從構想中的架構，轉為一筆完成且有可觀察需求的交易。

市政債與Anthropic融資之間的差異值得注意。Alphabet交易把高評等科技公司與公用事業長期採購連結，在免稅市場取得強勁需求；Anthropic融資則需要專門設立的載體、差異化的優先債保障，以及票息8.5%、無擔保支持的次順位層。兩者都支應AI所需的能源與硬體，但投資人對付款風險及剩餘價值風險的不同形式給出迥異定價。

困境信用市場週末也有獨立進展。Raizen就約650億巴西里爾、即$126億債務達成庭外重整協議。納入計畫的債務中，持有75.5%的債權人已表態支持，涉及19家金融機構及80名重要債券持有人；公司預計支持率至週一將超過80%。

協議將受影響債務的45%轉為股權，其餘55%換成新債，並要求Raizen在2027年底前把甘蔗加工事業與燃料經銷業務分拆。Raizen與Cosan的合資夥伴Shell支持這項計畫，且已承諾注資35億巴西里爾。

治理安排也是重整的一環。財務長Lorival Luz將兼任重整長，現任董事會預定留任至2027年第1季。董事長Rubens Ometto能否繼續留在董事會，則取決於是否注資5億巴西里爾。協議在6月8日法律期限前達成，降低近期聲請破產保護的風險，但實施仍須完成債權人及法院程序。

主權信用方面，週五稍晚亦出現評等事件。Morningstar DBRS把奧地利評等由AAA降至AA（high），展望穩定，使奧地利失去歐洲央行擔保品評估所採用五家機構中的最後一個最高評等。DBRS指出，儘管政府提出財政整頓計畫，財政赤字仍持續擴大、支出增加，債務比率預計也會緩步上升。

評等行動前，市場影響有限。奧地利10年期公債殖利率較可比德債高24個基點，仍低於過去10年平均利差。不過，財政部長Markus Marterbauer即將提出兩年期預算，政府面臨更具體的財政考驗。執政聯盟目標是在2028年前把赤字降至GDP的3%以下，並脫離歐盟財政監督；同時，高能源及勞動成本仍在限制競爭力。

日本企業面對的則是發展較慢的槓桿問題。截至3月止會計年度，已公布業績的日經225成分企業債務達¥678兆，較一年前增加4.6%，原因是收購、資本支出及股東分配消耗現金。標普在2025年調降19家日本大型企業評等，高於前一年的7家；穆迪也記錄19起調降，高於前一年的5起。

日本製鐵為融資$140億收購美國鋼鐵，現金部位減少約三分之一、借款倍增，成為標普降評原因之一。日本近期部分槓桿收購的債務倍數高達EBITDA的11倍，相較之下，亞洲區域常態為4.5倍以下。銀行大致仍符合資本指引，企業也保有可觀流動性；但市場預期日本央行升息、長天期日本公債殖利率走高，促使借款人偏好較短期限，把更多再融資風險移向曲線前端。

## 全球利率面對通膨與財政壓力

日本薪資數據強化日本央行在6月15日至16日會議升息的理由。4月實質薪資年增1.9%，高於1.7%的預測，也快於3月修正後的1.4%；連續第四個月上升，為四年來最長紀錄。名目薪資增加3.5%，高於3.1%的市場共識；基本薪資成長3.4%。日本央行官員關注、旨在降低抽樣失真的一項指標顯示，全職勞工薪資成長2.6%。

薪資改善讓日本央行總裁植田和男有證據可證明，今年春季勞資談判結果正逐步反映到家庭所得，也支持決策委員認為物價上行風險可能早於成長下行風險浮現的擔憂。市場普遍預期6月升息25個基點，官員也在考慮2026年稍後進一步行動的空間。

家庭需求仍是限制。4月實質支出年減0.5%，連續第五個月下降，食品、水電、服飾與鞋類支出均減少。6月預定漲價的食品與飲料超過1,000項，5月僅84項，生產者成本也已大幅上升。政府對電力、天然氣及汽油的補貼或能壓低統計通膨，卻無法消除企業利潤率壓力，也不能排除實質薪資今年稍後再度轉弱的風險。

印度央行選擇保持克制，未立即緊縮。印度儲備銀行一致決議把附買回利率維持在5.25%，符合預期，政策立場也維持中性。常設存款機制利率維持5.00%，邊際常設融資及銀行利率均維持5.50%。主要變化是把2026至2027財政年度消費者通膨預測由4.6%上調至5.1%。

這項決定承認通膨風險上升，但尚未認定已有升息必要。2026年以來，盧比兌美元已貶值約6%，企業也因債券殖利率上升而轉向銀行借款。另有措施旨在方便外資購買政府債券及股票，並降低外國機構投資債券的資本利得稅，以便在政策利率不變之際支持資本流入。

台灣5月通膨數據顯示，消費端與生產端均有壓力。消費者物價較4月上漲0.19%，年增2.20%，較先前1.74%的年增率加速。生產者物價月減0.07%，但年增14.11%，高於先前的8.54%。以美元計價，進口物價年增17.21%，出口物價上升18.09%；即使生產者物價指數按月微降，外部成本訊號仍然強烈。

哥倫比亞通膨則更直接挑戰其政策路徑。年通膨率由5.68%加速至5.84%，為2024年以來最快，僅略低於5.9%的預測中位數。消費者物價月增0.47%，決策官員關注的一項核心指標升至5.79%；燃料、租金、食品與餐飲是年增主因。

哥倫比亞央行4月在總統Gustavo Petro與財政部長牽涉的制度爭議下，意外把利率維持在11.25%。法院其後裁定，即使財政部長缺席，會議仍可舉行，排除了6月30日決策前的一項程序障礙。通膨加速提高恢復升息的壓力，不過會議將在6月21日總統決選後舉行。

歐洲的爭論已從歐洲央行會否在6月11日升息，轉向之後還會升息多少。歐元區5月通膨率達3.2%，核心通膨也高於預期；貨幣市場幾乎完全反映6月升息25個基點，交易員並押注年底前最多緊縮75個基點。

是否連續升息仍有爭議。摩根大通資產管理認為，成長疲弱可能使首次升息成為僅此一次的行動；Pictet及Carmignac則表示，維持利率不變也有充分理由。其論點部分來自市場通膨預期的反轉：1年後起算1年期通膨交換由2月底的1.75%，在伊朗戰爭爆發後升至2.40%，隨後回落至2.12%，僅略高於歐洲央行2%的目標。

成長數據也支持審慎立場。修正後資料顯示，歐元區第1季GDP並非成長，而是萎縮；OECD預測2026年僅成長0.8%。單次升息25個基點或許仍是該經濟體可以承受的幅度，但在高能源價格削弱家庭與企業需求之際，反覆緊縮將形成更顯著的壓力。

相反論點是，官員不能假設能源衝擊只會短暫存在。歐洲央行預計隨新預測公布不同衝突情境，總裁Christine Lagarde的指引將決定首次行動會被定位為保險，還是一輪升息循環的起點。許多機構的預測已納入再升息一次，市場定價反映的緊縮幅度則更大。這項差異將決定歐洲短端殖利率是否維持緊縮溢價，以及疲弱成長最終會否帶來前端反彈。

新興市場債券也面臨類似分歧：油價下跌可能帶來助益，但財政及通膨壓力仍持續。週末發布的研究顯示，自伊朗戰爭爆發以來，南韓、巴西、南非及墨西哥的長端殖利率均上升逾40個基點。新興市場通膨意外指數升至2022年10月以來最高，各國政府也因燃料與食品補貼承擔額外財政成本。

因此，和平協議可能使短天期債券比長債受益更多。能源價格下降會降低央行近期升息壓力，但公共借款、國防支出、能源安全投資及AI基礎設施仍會影響期限溢價。南韓10年期殖利率接近逾兩年高點4.25%，背景包括可能發行追加預算債券、通膨疑慮及半導體帶動的成長。巴西基準殖利率則維持在14%以上，公共部門總債務自疫情以來首次突破GDP的80%。

印尼的信心問題更為嚴峻。當地股市基準指數較五個月前創下的高點下跌近39%；印尼盾2026年已貶值約8%，貶破1美元兌18,000印尼盾。今年外資已淨撤出$4.22億印尼債券及$35.6億股票；財政干預、商品出口規則及主權信用疑慮，進一步加重全球避險潮的影響。

印尼央行與財政部週末表示，將維持市場流動性、支撐殖利率並鼓勵資金流入。央行也計畫提高政府存放於央行之存款的報酬。分析師指出，這項措施可能有助抵銷政府利息負擔，但仍需說明利率、存款規模及對債券發行的影響，避免政策被視為模糊財政與貨幣職責的界線。

中國外匯存底數據則提供較穩定的外部訊號。5月底官方外匯存底較4月的$3.4105兆增加$317億、即0.93%，至$3.4422兆。國家外匯管理局把增幅歸因於匯率換算及全球資產價格變動，而未視為干預或資本流動的直接指標。因此，數據上的存底緩衝有所增強，但仍無法判斷底層私人資金流出的方向。

## 後續市場意義

美國5月CPI將於6月10日美東時間08:30公布，是非農帶動重新定價後第一項決定性考驗。市場共識預期整體CPI月增0.5%、年增4.2%，前值分別為0.6%及3.8%；核心CPI月增率則預期由0.4%放緩至0.3%。通膨交換顯示年增率可能約為4.3%。核心價格壓力的廣度，將決定實質殖利率能否在通膨補償未同步上升下維持漲勢。

生產者物價將於6月11日美東時間08:30接續公布。市場預測整體及核心指數分別月增0.6%與0.5%，前值為1.4%及1.0%。納入聯準會偏好PCE指標的分項，重要性將高於整體數字本身。同一時間也會公布截至6月6日當週的初領失業救濟金人數，這是非農後首項高頻勞動市場檢驗；此前一週為22.5萬人。

整段數據公布期間，美債供給將同時考驗政策敏感期限與長天期債券。政府將於6月8日標售$890億13週期國庫券及$770億26週期國庫券，6月11日交割。6月9日則標售$650億6週期國庫券、$500億52週期國庫券，以及$580億新發3年期公債。3年期是非農後首次附息債標售，將顯示前端殖利率急升後，投資人能否順利吸收規模不變的供給。

6月9日的流動性支持回購，最多可能接受$20億於2036年6月至2046年6月到期的名目附息債。財政部之後將於6月10日CPI公布後增額發行$390億10年期公債，並在6月11日PPI、初領失業救濟金及歐洲央行決策公布後，增額發行$220億30年期公債。10年期與30年期結果將檢驗，週五長端殖利率相對溫和的漲幅究竟反映持久需求，還是只因前端對非農更敏感。6月11日另有一筆現金管理回購，最多可能接受$125億於2026年7月至2028年6月到期的附息債。

歐洲央行將於6月11日美東時間08:15公布決策，Lagarde於08:45舉行記者會，是最重要的全球政策事件。市場共識預期存款利率上升25個基點至2.25%，主要再融資利率及邊際放款利率分別升至2.40%及2.65%。更重要的市場問題是，官員會支持進一步緊縮的預期，還是強調經濟萎縮及短期通膨交換回落。

加拿大央行於6月10日決策，市場共識傾向連續第五次把利率維持在2.25%。決策須權衡能源驅動的通膨、第1季經濟萎縮，以及其後5月就業增加87,800人。中國同日稍早公布5月消費者及生產者物價；市場預期CPI年增1.4%、PPI年增3.5%，前值分別為1.2%及2.8%。這些數據將顯示全球能源及工廠成本衝擊，是否正擴及另一個主要製造業經濟體。

本週最後的重要數據包括6月12日密西根大學消費者信心初值，市場預期由44.8升至46.5；印度CPI則預期由3.48%加速至4.00%。日本生產者物價將在日本央行6月15日至16日會議前，再提供一項成本壓力指標；聯準會隨後於6月16日至17日開會。屆時，投資人將綜合通膨、初領失業救濟金及完整一輪附息債標售的結果，判斷非農意外究竟標誌持久緊縮階段的開端，還是本輪政策重新定價的高點，仍可由較溫和的物價數據逆轉。

overall_summary.headline: 非農強勁逆轉美債漲勢，市場完全反映聯準會年底前升息
overall_summary.session_narrative:
5月非農就業增加17.2萬人，高於所有預測，前期數字上修，失業率維持4.3%，美債因而逆轉前一交易日漲勢。2年期殖利率上升10.3個基點至4.148%，10年期及30年期分別上升5.6與2.1個基點；曲線隨前端領跌而趨平，交易員並已完全反映聯準會12月前升息。

## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

A much stronger-than-expected U.S. employment report reversed the previous session’s Treasury rally on June 5, pulled the policy-sensitive front end sharply higher and left traders fully pricing a Federal Reserve rate increase by year-end. Nonfarm payrolls rose 172,000 in May, exceeding every forecast, while March and April hiring was revised upward and unemployment held at 4.3%. The breadth of hiring challenged the view that the economy was settling into a low-hire equilibrium just as elevated energy costs were keeping inflation above the Fed’s objective.

The 2-year yield rose 10.3 basis points to 4.148%, the 5-year increased 8.4 basis points to 4.269%, the 10-year added 5.6 basis points to 4.531% and the 30-year climbed 2.1 basis points to 4.997%. The front-end-led move flattened 2s10s by 4.7 basis points to 38.3 basis points and 2s30s by 8.2 basis points to 84.9 basis points. That configuration located the immediate shock in the expected policy path rather than in a new long-end concession for fiscal supply or persistent inflation.

The 10-year decomposition strengthened that reading. The real yield rose 7.1 basis points to 2.162%, more than the increase in the nominal yield, while the 10-year breakeven declined 1.5 basis points to 2.369%. WTI crude fell 2.69% to $90.54 and Brent declined 2.04% to $93.09, allowing inflation compensation to ease even as the labor report increased the real rate investors required. The selloff was therefore not a simple extension of the energy-driven inflation trade. Payrolls showed that demand could withstand current borrowing costs, reducing the Fed’s freedom to look through the price shock.

The adjustment spread far beyond government bonds. The dollar index gained 0.66%, gold futures fell 3.10%, the S&P 500 lost 2.64% and the Nasdaq 100 dropped 4.77%. The PHLX Semiconductor Index plunged 10.26%, while the VIX rose nearly 40% to 21.51. The violence in technology shares reflected more than the payroll surprise: investors were also questioning elevated AI valuations and the scale of capital still required to fund the build-out. Higher real yields turned those concerns into a broad reassessment of long-duration equity risk.

Federal Reserve Bank of Cleveland President Beth Hammack said the report reaffirmed that the labor market was roughly in balance and that 4.3% unemployment was close to her definition of full employment. She still favored holding rates steady amid uncertainty, but repeated that it might soon be appropriate to act if recent trends continued. That conditional warning gained force from the data, even as forecasters remained divided over whether the next move would actually be an increase. BNP Paribas projected three hikes beginning in December, while Citigroup retained three cuts for 2026 and Goldman Sachs removed its final expected 2026 cut without making a hike its base case.

The close thus combined a decisive near-term repricing with an unresolved medium-term policy argument. Payroll breadth, upward revisions and firm consumer borrowing made labor weakness a less credible reason for easing. Falling oil and lower breakevens, however, showed that investors had not simply extrapolated the latest energy shock into long-run inflation. The next judgment turns on whether May consumer and producer prices validate the market’s new tightening path, and whether Treasury demand remains orderly through $119 billion of coupon auctions.

## Payroll Breadth Reprices the Fed Path

The payroll gain of 172,000 compared with a pre-release median forecast of 88,000 and followed upward revisions to each of the previous two months. Together, the three months produced the strongest hiring advance in more than two years. That sequence was more important than a single upside headline because it replaced a picture of near-stagnant employment with evidence that the labor market had been strengthening across several reports.

Unemployment remained at 4.3%, participation was unchanged at 61.8% and the participation rate among workers aged 25 to 54 edged higher. A broader unemployment measure, which includes discouraged workers and people working part-time for economic reasons, declined. Those details left little evidence that the payroll increase was masking deterioration in labor supply or underemployment.

Hiring was also broader than the concentration in defensive service industries that had supported employment during earlier soft patches. Leisure and hospitality added 70,000 jobs, the most in more than three years, led by restaurants and bars. Healthcare and social assistance continued to expand at a firm pace, while manufacturing also added workers and nonresidential construction employment increased for a seventh month.

Some of that strength may prove temporary. Economists said preparations for the FIFA World Cup in June and July may have lifted leisure and hospitality employment, and such hiring could slow or unwind after the event. Information-sector employment also fell for the 16th time in 17 months as large technology companies reduced headcount while committing more capital to AI infrastructure. Small businesses had been scaling back hiring plans, and consumer assessments of job availability remained weaker than in recent years.

The distinguishing feature of May was that these qualifications did not overwhelm the broader advance. Factory demand tied to data centers, defense production and precautionary stockbuilding supported manufacturing. Construction spending on data centers had exceeded $50 billion at an annualized rate in April for the first time, accounting for 2.3% of all U.S. construction spending. Nonresidential construction hiring therefore provided another link between the capital-investment boom and the labor market rather than merely reflecting residential or public works activity.

The Treasury response was immediate. In intraday trading after the release, the 2-year yield rose about 11 basis points to 4.15% and subsequently reached as high as 4.17%. The completed daily observation left it at 4.148%, still 10.3 basis points above the previous day and 20.5 basis points higher than a month earlier. The 5-year sector also bore much of the adjustment, leaving the curve flatter as traders moved from assigning a high probability of a year-end increase to fully pricing a quarter-point move.

Interest-rate swaps indicated roughly a 60% probability that an increase could arrive in October, though the full quarter-point was priced only by the December meeting. That distinction matters because the June 16-17 meeting is still widely expected to leave the federal funds target at 3.5% to 3.75%. The immediate market question is less whether the Fed will raise rates in June than whether it will remove the easing bias from its statement and establish an explicitly two-sided path for subsequent meetings.

The jobs report altered that communication problem. Earlier evidence had shown a rise in jobless claims, contracting employment readings in services surveys and a low-hire, low-fire environment. May payrolls did not invalidate every softer indicator, but the upward revisions and stronger sector breadth made an imminent employment break harder to treat as the central case. Policymakers can now concentrate more directly on inflation without appearing to neglect a rapidly weakening labor mandate.

Consumer credit supplied a separate demand and balance-sheet signal later in the session. Borrowing increased by $20.73 billion in April, above the $17.80 billion consensus and following a revised $22.23 billion March gain. Total consumer credit outstanding reached $5.1531 trillion and expanded at a 4.8% annualized rate. Revolving credit grew 10.4%, compared with 2.9% for nonrevolving balances.

The acceleration in revolving borrowing is not unambiguously strong demand, because households can also rely on credit when income growth is insufficient. Even so, it showed continued access to unsecured financing and no abrupt pullback in household borrowing. Alongside the jobs result, it denied the Fed a clean demand-destruction signal before the next inflation releases.

Treasury turnover reflected the size of the repricing. FINRA recorded $1.174 trillion of par activity across 429,057 trades, with total par volume up 12.9% from the previous day. Nominal-coupon activity rose 24.3% to $999.2 billion. Trading in coupons with more than 3 and up to 5 years remaining increased 39.7% to $277.9 billion, the largest increase among the detailed maturity buckets, while activity at 2 years and shorter rose 18.8% and the 7- to 10-year sector increased 18.4%. The concentration confirms that the policy-sensitive belly was the center of trading, without identifying whether customers were net buyers or sellers.

Weekly futures data showed that the repricing entered a market with large opposing positions rather than a clean directional consensus. As of June 2, asset managers held substantial net-long exposures across Treasury contracts, while leveraged funds were heavily net short. Asset-manager net positions had increased by 190,077 contracts in 5-year futures and 283,949 in 10-year futures over the week, while leveraged funds added 186,242 contracts to their net 5-year short. Those positions predated payrolls and cannot establish the direction of Friday’s flows, but they indicate why a large data surprise could generate rapid adjustment across the curve.

## Real Yields Drive a Violent Risk Reversal

The Treasury selloff was dominated by real yields even though the market’s broader inflation concern remained rooted in the Middle East energy shock. The 10-year real yield rose to 2.162%, up 21.8 basis points over one month. The 10-year breakeven, by contrast, fell to 2.369%, 11.2 basis points lower over the same period. Investors were demanding a higher inflation-adjusted return as resilient activity raised the expected policy rate, while requiring less—not more—long-horizon inflation compensation.

Oil’s decline helped produce that separation. WTI ended at $90.54 and Brent at $93.09, although both remained higher over the week. The fall eased the immediate inflation impulse without resolving the conflict-related disruption to energy flows. It also meant that payrolls, rather than another daily rise in crude, provided the clearest explanation for the Treasury move.

The 2s30s curve’s 8.2-basis-point flattening was especially instructive. The 30-year yield briefly moved back above 5% in market reporting but finished at 4.997%, only 2.1 basis points higher on the day. If the session had principally represented a new fiscal, supply or long-run inflation shock, greater pressure at the long end would have been more likely. Instead, the largest losses occurred where expected Fed policy has the most direct influence.

That real-rate repricing struck an equity market that had become highly dependent on long-duration growth assumptions. Before June 5, the Nasdaq 100 had risen more than 30% since March 30. The 4.77% daily drop was its worst since April 2025, while the semiconductor index’s 10.26% fall erased much of its weekly advance. Information-technology shares in the S&P 500 declined 5.8%, but five of the benchmark’s 11 sectors rose, led by consumer staples and utilities. The dispersion showed a rotation away from expensive technology exposure rather than a uniform collapse in current economic expectations.

Company-specific doubts intensified the move. Broadcom’s revenue forecast disappointed investors, while a report that Meta Platforms was considering an equity raise renewed questions about whether even the largest technology companies could internally fund the AI investment cycle. Those concerns landed on the same day that higher real yields increased the discount rate applied to distant earnings and the payroll report reduced the prospect of near-term monetary relief.

The risk reduction extended to other assets. Gold futures fell to $4,337.10, down 3.10%, as the combination of higher real rates and a stronger dollar outweighed its haven role. Bitcoin fell below $60,000 during the session for the first time since October 2024. The dollar index rose to 100.07, and all Group-of-10 currencies weakened against the U.S. currency after the employment data.

Listed credit funds declined without showing the same scale of dislocation as technology equities. The investment-grade LQD fund lost 0.62%, high-yield funds HYG and JNK fell 0.50% and 0.44%, respectively, and the emerging-market debt fund EMB declined 0.73%. Those returns combined duration and underlying credit effects and do not establish a broad spread move. They do show that fixed-income risk assets did not escape the simultaneous rise in Treasury yields and fall in equities.

## Warsh Faces a Faster Policy Debate

Hammack’s response made the payroll report an explicit input to the Fed’s reaction function. She said the labor market appeared roughly balanced and described the 4.3% unemployment rate as close to full employment. Holding rates steady remained reasonable because of uncertainty, but continued recent trends could soon justify action. Her condition was unchanged from remarks earlier in the week; the new information was that payrolls had moved materially in the direction that makes the condition easier to satisfy.

The first meeting under Chairman Kevin Warsh will consequently require more than an uneventful hold. April minutes showed that a majority of officials believed an increase might need to be considered if inflation remained persistently above 2%. Governors Lisa Cook and Christopher Waller, who had supported easing previously, had also said recently that inflation was moving in the wrong direction and might eventually warrant higher rates. The May employment result weakened the labor-market argument against that shift.

Warsh has not yet publicly set out his policy view since taking office. Before his nomination, he had a reputation as an inflation hawk but had also argued that rates should be cut and pointed to forces he believed would support lower borrowing costs over time. His June press conference must reconcile that history with an economy showing stronger hiring and an April reading of 3.8% for the Fed’s preferred inflation measure, the highest since 2023.

The economic forecasts released at the meeting will add another communication test. They are likely to embody higher inflation and rate assumptions than the March projections, but the evidence does not establish how many officials will project increases or when. The jobs report makes it easier to remove language favoring a cut; it does not by itself settle whether the committee will adopt an overt tightening bias.

Wall Street forecasts now span unusually different reaction functions. BNP Paribas expects the Fed to begin raising rates in December and ultimately reverse the 75 basis points of easing delivered in 2025 through three successive increases. An earlier start remains possible in its view if the labor market stays strong and the Iran conflict sustains inflation. That forecast treats the prior easing as insurance that may need to be withdrawn once the economy proves more resilient than expected.

Citigroup maintained the opposite call. Chief U.S. economist Andrew Hollenhorst expects the labor market to weaken over the next three months, leading the Fed to cut by 25 basis points at each of its September, October and December meetings. Citi acknowledged that June officials would focus more heavily on upside inflation risk after the payroll report, but argued that current strength would not persist.

Goldman Sachs moved between those poles in a Friday note. It abandoned a December 2026 cut and shifted its final two expected reductions to June and December 2027. The bank raised the probability of modest rate increases to 20% from 10%, but still judged hikes unlikely because inflation appeared less likely to become self-sustaining. It assigned only a 30% probability to its new two-cut 2027 baseline and described an extended period of unchanged rates as a plausible alternative. Goldman also lowered its 2026 unemployment forecast to 4.4% from 4.6%.

The divergence turns on more than the next inflation print. BNP sees a strong economy that may require the Fed to withdraw earlier easing; Citi expects labor weakness to re-emerge; Goldman sees enough inflation restraint to avoid hikes but not enough weakness to justify a 2026 cut. Payrolls moved the market toward the first view, while the fall in breakevens and oil preserved room for the latter two.

Political pressure became more explicit after the close. In an interview recorded Friday and aired Sunday, President Donald Trump said the Fed would be wrong to raise rates and should instead lower them. He argued that economic success should not automatically be penalized with tighter policy and linked his preference for lower rates to federal debt and plans for greater military spending. Because the interview aired after the completed session, it did not cause Friday’s repricing. It does sharpen the institutional test facing Warsh at his debut meeting: markets have moved toward tightening while the president who nominated him is publicly demanding the opposite.

## Credit Markets Fund AI While Distress Restructures

The technology selloff did not stop large AI-related financing from reaching completion. Apollo Global Management and Blackstone finalized a $35 billion package to purchase Google-designed chips that Anthropic will lease, one of the largest private-credit transactions yet assembled. Roughly half the debt was syndicated to outside investors, showing the scale of institutional demand required even when major alternative-asset managers originate the structure.

The package divided risk across three tranches. A $6 billion A1 layer was sold to banks at a coupon 1 percentage point over Treasuries. A $24 billion A2 tranche priced at par with a 5.75% coupon and attracted institutional buyers including Apollo’s Athene insurance business. Both senior tranches carried private mid-investment-grade ratings and received payment support from Broadcom.

The remaining $4.5 billion of B notes lacked the Broadcom backing and priced at par with an 8.5% coupon. The 275-basis-point difference from the A2 coupon showed how much value investors placed on the additional protection, although the tranches may also differ in other structural respects. The transaction’s economics depend primarily on lease payments generated by chips held in a special-purpose vehicle and on their residual value if Anthropic fails to pay.

Broadcom’s support addresses that residual-value risk for the senior debt. If lease payments cease for a specified period, the vehicle can sell the chips. Broadcom has agreed to cover any remaining shortfall owed to A1 and A2 investors, up to 100% of their protected amount. The B notes do not receive that support. The structure allows the senior layers to borrow closer to Broadcom’s credit profile while leaving junior investors directly exposed to the value of specialized hardware and Anthropic’s lease performance.

The financing is expected to be the first of several transactions under an AI infrastructure platform involving Broadcom, Apollo, Blackstone and other investors. Broadcom said the platform aims to deploy more than 20 gigawatts of computing capacity through 2028. That prospective pipeline matters for fixed income because it converts an equity-market growth theme into repeated demand for bank balance sheets, private credit, insurance capital and structured debt.

Municipal investors supplied another route for technology-linked financing. A roughly $1 billion prepaid-energy issue involving Alphabet and Pioneer Community Energy drew strong secondary demand after pricing. The California Community Choice Financing Authority issued the bonds, Goldman Sachs underwrote them and Alphabet served as the financial intermediary in the prepaid electricity arrangement.

The largest portion initially priced 95 basis points above its benchmark. It subsequently traded at tighter spreads, and the 2035 maturity alone recorded $492 million of trades by Friday afternoon. Those bonds traded at an average spread of 89 basis points, with some transactions as tight as 74 basis points. The result moved Alphabet’s entry into prepaid-energy finance from a prospective structure to a completed transaction with observable demand.

The contrast between the muni issue and the Anthropic package was useful. Alphabet’s transaction linked a highly rated technology name to long-term utility procurement and obtained strong demand in the tax-exempt market. The Anthropic financing required a purpose-built vehicle, differentiated senior support and an 8.5% unguaranteed junior layer. Both funded the energy and hardware needs of AI, but investors priced very different forms of payment and residual-value risk.

Distressed credit supplied a separate weekend development. Raizen reached an out-of-court restructuring agreement covering about 65 billion reais, or $12.6 billion, of debt. Creditors holding 75.5% of the obligations included in the plan supported the agreement, which involves 19 financial institutions and 80 significant bondholders. The company expected support to exceed 80% by Monday.

The agreement converts 45% of the affected debt into equity and exchanges the remaining 55% for new debt. It also calls for Raizen’s sugarcane-processing business to be separated from its fuel-distribution operation by the end of 2027. Shell, Raizen’s joint-venture partner with Cosan, supports the plan and had already committed a 3.5 billion-real capital injection.

Governance remains part of the restructuring. Chief Financial Officer Lorival Luz will also become chief restructuring officer, while the current board is scheduled to remain through the first quarter of 2027. Chairman Rubens Ometto’s continued board role remains contingent on a 500 million-real capital injection. The agreement was reached before a June 8 legal deadline and reduces the immediate risk of a bankruptcy-protection filing, but implementation still requires creditor and court processes.

Sovereign credit also registered a late-Friday rating event. Morningstar DBRS cut Austria to AA (high) from AAA and assigned a stable outlook, removing the country’s last top rating from one of the five agencies used by the ECB for collateral assessment. DBRS cited persistently wider fiscal deficits, higher expenditure and a debt ratio expected to continue rising slowly despite consolidation plans.

The market impact had been limited before the action. Austria’s 10-year bonds yielded 24 basis points more than comparable German debt, below their 10-year average spread. The government nevertheless faces a more concrete fiscal test when Finance Minister Markus Marterbauer presents a two-year budget. The coalition aims to lower the deficit below 3% of GDP by 2028 and exit EU fiscal scrutiny, while high energy and labor costs continue to constrain competitiveness.

Corporate Japan faces a slower-moving version of the leverage problem. Debt among Nikkei 225 companies reporting for the fiscal year through March reached ¥678 trillion, 4.6% more than a year earlier, as acquisitions, capital spending and shareholder distributions consumed cash. S&P downgraded 19 major Japanese companies in 2025, compared with seven a year earlier; Moody’s also recorded 19 reductions, up from five.

Nippon Steel’s cash position fell by about a third and its borrowings doubled while it financed the $14 billion acquisition of U.S. Steel, contributing to an S&P downgrade. Some recent Japanese leveraged buyouts reached debt multiples as high as 11 times EBITDA, compared with a regional Asian norm of 4.5 times or less. Banks remain broadly within capital guidance and companies still hold substantial liquidity, but prospective BOJ increases and higher long-government yields are encouraging borrowers to favor shorter maturities, transferring more refinancing exposure toward the front of the curve.

## Global Rates Confront Inflation and Fiscal Pressure

Japan’s wage data strengthened the case for a BOJ increase at its June 15-16 meeting. Real wages rose 1.9% from a year earlier in April, above the 1.7% forecast and faster than the revised 1.4% gain in March. The fourth consecutive increase was the longest run in four years. Nominal earnings rose 3.5%, exceeding the 3.1% consensus, while base pay increased 3.4%. A measure designed to reduce sampling distortions and monitored by BOJ officials showed a 2.6% gain for full-time workers.

The wage improvement gives Governor Kazuo Ueda evidence that this year’s spring pay agreements are reaching household income. It also supports the board’s concern that upside price risks may be arriving sooner than downside growth risks. A quarter-point June increase is widely expected, and officials are also considering the scope for further moves later in 2026.

Household demand remains the qualification. Real spending fell 0.5% from a year earlier in April, the fifth consecutive decline, with lower outlays on food, utilities, clothing and footwear. More than 1,000 food and beverage products were scheduled for price increases in June, compared with 84 in May, while producer costs had risen sharply. Government electricity, gas and gasoline subsidies may restrain measured inflation, but they do not remove the pressure on corporate margins or the risk that real wages weaken again later in the year.

India’s central bank chose restraint rather than immediate tightening. The Reserve Bank of India unanimously held the repo rate at 5.25%, in line with expectations, and retained a neutral stance. The standing deposit facility stayed at 5.00%, while the marginal standing facility and Bank Rate remained at 5.50%. The significant change was a rise in the RBI’s FY2026-27 consumer-inflation forecast to 5.1% from 4.6%.

The decision acknowledges higher inflation risk without concluding that an increase was already necessary. It also arrives as the rupee has fallen about 6% against the dollar during 2026 and companies have shifted toward bank borrowing as bond yields rose. Separate steps to make government bonds and equities easier for foreign investors to buy, together with a reduction in capital-gains taxes on bond investments by foreign institutions, seek to support capital inflows alongside the unchanged policy rate.

Taiwan’s May inflation data showed pressure at both consumer and producer levels. Consumer prices rose 0.19% from April and 2.20% from a year earlier, accelerating from a 1.74% annual rate. Producer prices fell 0.07% on the month but increased 14.11% from a year earlier, compared with 8.54% previously. In U.S.-dollar terms, import prices rose 17.21% annually and export prices increased 18.09%, preserving a strong external cost signal even though the monthly producer index edged down.

Colombia recorded a more direct challenge to its policy path. Annual inflation accelerated to 5.84% from 5.68%, the fastest since 2024 and only slightly below the 5.9% median forecast. Consumer prices rose 0.47% on the month, and a core measure followed by policymakers increased to 5.79%. Fuel, rents, food and restaurants led the annual advance.

The central bank had unexpectedly held its rate at 11.25% in April amid an institutional dispute involving President Gustavo Petro and the finance minister. A court has since ruled that meetings can proceed without the finance minister, removing one procedural obstacle before the June 30 decision. The inflation acceleration increases pressure to resume hikes, although the meeting will occur after the June 21 presidential runoff.

In Europe, the debate has moved beyond whether the ECB will raise rates on June 11 to how far it will go afterward. Euro-area inflation reached 3.2% in May, with core inflation also stronger than anticipated, while money markets nearly fully priced a 25-basis-point increase at the June meeting. Traders favored as much as 75 basis points of tightening by year-end.

The case for a sequence remains contested. JPMorgan Asset Management argued that weak growth could make the first increase a one-and-done move, while Pictet and Carmignac said holding rates steady would be defensible. Their argument rests partly on the reversal in market inflation expectations: the 1-year, 1-year inflation swap rose from 1.75% at the end of February to 2.40% after the Iran war began, but subsequently retreated to 2.12%, only modestly above the ECB’s 2% objective.

Growth evidence supports the caution. Revised data showed that euro-area GDP contracted in the first quarter rather than expanding, and the OECD expects only 0.8% growth in 2026. A single 25-basis-point increase may be manageable for that economy; repeated tightening would impose a more consequential restraint just as high energy prices weaken household and corporate demand.

The opposing case is that officials cannot assume the energy shock will remain temporary. The ECB is expected to publish alternative conflict scenarios with its new forecasts, and President Christine Lagarde’s guidance will determine whether the initial move is presented as insurance or the beginning of a cycle. A further increase is already embedded in many forecasts, while the market prices more. The distinction will determine whether short European yields retain their tightening premium and whether weak growth eventually produces a front-end rally.

Emerging-market duration faces a similar split between the likely benefit of lower oil and the persistence of fiscal and inflation pressure. Research published over the weekend found that long yields in South Korea, Brazil, South Africa and Mexico had risen more than 40 basis points since the Iran war began. An index of inflation surprises across emerging markets reached its highest since October 2022, while governments incurred additional fiscal costs from fuel and food support.

A peace agreement could therefore benefit shorter maturities more than long bonds. Lower energy prices would reduce immediate pressure for central-bank increases, but public borrowing, defense spending, energy-security investment and AI infrastructure would continue to affect term premiums. South Korea’s 10-year yield was near a more than two-year high of 4.25% amid prospective supplementary-budget issuance, inflation concern and semiconductor-led growth. Brazilian benchmark yields remained above 14% as gross public debt exceeded 80% of GDP for the first time since the pandemic.

Indonesia presents the more acute confidence problem. Its stock benchmark has fallen nearly 39% from a record reached five months earlier, and the rupiah has weakened about 8% in 2026, breaching 18,000 per dollar. Foreign investors have withdrawn a net $422 million from Indonesian bonds and $3.56 billion from equities this year as fiscal intervention, commodity-export rules and sovereign-credit concerns compounded the global retreat from risk.

Bank Indonesia and the finance ministry said over the weekend that they would maintain market liquidity, support yields and encourage capital inflows. The central bank also plans to increase the remuneration paid on government deposits held with it. Analysts said the measure could help offset the government’s interest burden but warned that details on the rate, deposit scale and implications for bond issuance are needed to prevent the policy from being viewed as a blurring of fiscal and monetary responsibilities.

China’s reserve data offered a steadier external signal. Official foreign-exchange reserves rose by $31.7 billion, or 0.93%, to $3.4422 trillion at the end of May from $3.4105 trillion in April. SAFE attributed the increase to currency translation and changes in global asset prices, rather than treating it as a direct measure of intervention or capital flows. The rise therefore strengthened the measured reserve buffer without resolving the direction of underlying private outflows.

## Forward Market Significance

The May U.S. CPI release at 08:30 ET on June 10 is the first decisive test of the payroll-driven repricing. Consensus expects headline inflation to rise 0.5% on the month and 4.2% from a year earlier, after 0.6% and 3.8%, while core inflation is expected to slow to 0.3% monthly from 0.4%. Inflation swaps were indicating an annual reading around 4.3%. The breadth of core pressure will determine whether the rise in real yields can be sustained without a corresponding increase in inflation compensation.

Producer prices follow at 08:30 ET on June 11. Forecasts call for monthly increases of 0.6% in the headline index and 0.5% in the core measure, after 1.4% and 1.0%. Components feeding into the Fed’s preferred PCE index will matter more than the headline alone. Initial claims for the week ended June 6 arrive at the same time, providing the first high-frequency labor check after payrolls and following 225,000 claims in the prior week.

Treasury supply will test the policy-sensitive and long-duration sectors across that data sequence. The government will auction $89 billion of 13-week bills and $77 billion of 26-week bills on June 8, settling June 11. On June 9 it will sell $65 billion of 6-week bills, $50 billion of 52-week bills and $58 billion of new 3-year notes. The 3-year sale is the first coupon auction after payrolls and will show how readily investors absorb an unchanged offering after the sharp rise in front-end yields.

A liquidity-support buyback on June 9 may accept as much as $2 billion of nominal coupons maturing from June 2036 through June 2046. Treasury then reopens $39 billion of 10-year notes on June 10 after CPI and $22 billion of 30-year bonds on June 11 after PPI, claims and the ECB decision. The 10-year and 30-year results will test whether the relatively modest Friday rise in long yields reflects durable demand or merely the front end’s greater sensitivity to payrolls. A separate June 11 cash-management buyback may accept up to $12.5 billion of coupons maturing between July 2026 and June 2028.

The ECB decision at 08:15 ET on June 11, followed by Lagarde’s 08:45 press conference, is the principal global policy event. Consensus expects the deposit rate to rise 25 basis points to 2.25%, with the main refinancing and marginal lending rates increasing to 2.40% and 2.65%. The larger market question is whether officials validate expectations for further tightening or emphasize contracting activity and the retreat in near-term inflation swaps.

The Bank of Canada decides on June 10, with consensus favoring a fifth consecutive hold at 2.25%. The decision must weigh energy-driven inflation against a first-quarter contraction and a subsequent 87,800 increase in May employment. China publishes May consumer and producer prices earlier that day; consensus expects annual CPI inflation of 1.4% and PPI inflation of 3.5%, compared with 1.2% and 2.8%. Those releases will show whether the global energy and factory-cost shock is broadening across another major manufacturing economy.

The week closes with preliminary University of Michigan sentiment on June 12, where consensus expects an increase to 46.5 from 44.8, and Indian CPI, expected to accelerate to 4.00% from 3.48%. Japan’s producer-price data will provide another cost-pressure reading before the BOJ meets June 15-16. The Fed follows on June 16-17. By then, investors will have evidence from inflation, claims and the full coupon-auction cycle to judge whether the payroll surprise marked the start of a durable tightening phase or the high point of a policy repricing that softer prices can still reverse.

overall_summary.headline: Strong payrolls reverse the Treasury rally and fully price a Fed increase by year-end
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries reversed the previous session’s rally after May payrolls rose 172,000, beating every forecast, prior months were revised higher and unemployment held at 4.3%. The 2-year yield climbed 10.3 basis points to 4.148%, versus increases of 5.6 basis points in the 10-year and 2.1 basis points in the 30-year, flattening the curve as traders fully priced a Fed increase by December.

The 10-year real yield rose 7.1 basis points to 2.162%, while the breakeven fell 1.5 basis points to 2.369%. Falling crude prices helped inflation compensation ease, but stronger hiring and continued consumer borrowing reduced the Fed’s freedom to look through elevated price pressure. The adjustment spread into a stronger dollar, weaker gold and a sharp technology-led equity reversal as higher real yields compounded doubts about AI valuations and financing needs.

The close established a decisive near-term policy repricing without settling the medium-term path. May CPI and PPI will test whether inflation supports the new tightening expectations, while $119 billion of 10-year and 30-year coupon auctions will show whether long-end demand remains orderly.
